title: Understanding Recursion: The Power of Self-Calling Functions
key_points: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself to break a large problem into smaller, manageable pieces.
A 'Base Case' is mandatory; it acts as an exit strategy to prevent the function from running forever.
Each recursive call creates a new 'layer' of work, which is resolved once the base case is reached.
Recursion is often an elegant alternative to loops for tasks like navigating trees or sorting data.

title: Mastering REST APIs: Architectural Patterns and Practical Implementation
key_points: Resource-Oriented Architecture: Map your data model to URIs (e.g., /users/123/orders) rather than functional endpoints like /getUserOrders.
Statelessness and Scalability: By offloading state management to the client, servers become horizontally scalable, as any server instance can handle any request without prior context.
HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State): Advanced REST APIs include links in their responses to guide the client on available next steps, promoting loose coupling.
Idempotency: Ensure that repeated identical requests (like PUT or DELETE) result in the same server state as a single request, which is critical for network reliability.

title: Binary Search: Theoretical Foundations and Production-Grade Implementation
key_points: Integer Overflow: Calculating the midpoint as (low + high) / 2 can lead to integer overflow in languages with fixed-width integers; the robust alternative is low + (high - low) / 2.
Cache Locality vs. Dynamic Updates: Binary search provides excellent read performance and cache locality for static arrays but suffers from O(n) overhead for structural modifications.

Boundary Conditions: Off-by-one errors are the primary source of bugs; developers must strictly define whether the search space is [low, high] (inclusive) or [low, high) (half-open) and maintain the loop invariant consistently.
Branch Prediction: In tight loops, the conditional branching of binary search can lead to pipeline stalls on modern CPUs, though this is rarely the bottleneck compared to memory access latency.
